NO. 061 · The Kingfishers / Alcedinidae · Kingfishers

Pied Kingfisher

斑鱼狗 · bān yú gǒu Ceryle rudis
Resident Uncommon 25–30 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

Black and white, spotted, and the only kingfisher that hovers

The odd one out in the kingfisher family: black and white, without a trace of blue or green, and it hovers over the water like a helicopter before dropping vertically in. No other kingfisher does this.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • PlumageBlack and white throughout: upperparts boldly pied, white spots on the wing coverts, tail white with a black central band.
  • HeadA conspicuous black crest on the crown, a white supercilium, a black patch at the lores — the effect of a hat and drawn-on eyebrows.
  • Breast bandOne or two black bands across the breast — two in the male, one often incomplete in the female — the basis for sexing the bird.
  • BillBlack, long and pointed; the female's lower mandible usually shows some red.

Behaviour

Its feeding method is the most distinctive: it hovers three to ten metres above the water, head down, searching, then folds its wings and drops vertically, closing the eye behind the nictitating membrane an instant before entry. Usually in pairs or small parties, perching on waterside wires and dead branches. South China holds stable populations on creeks, reservoirs and fish ponds.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qianshan River
  • Qianwu Reservoir
  • Doumen tidal creeks
  • Hengqin wetland channels
Field note
A small black and white bird stopped dead in the air is a Pied Kingfisher hovering — the most immediate way to tell it from a Common Kingfisher.
